title: Slowsyrupy sloe
html_source: Sloes are little berries, about the size of a dime, that grow wild in hedgerows all over England. Ripe sloes may be lovely to look at, but their taste is highly astringent and generally unpleasant. The Brits have been making sloe gin for hundreds of years by infusing the berries in high-proof gin, along with a little bit of sugar. The result is a liqueur that’s tart, but with a delicious richness and depth of flavor.
